definitions.explanation: A ruler who holds absolute power over a country, typically one who has seized control by force or maintains power through authoritarian means.

examples.japanese: {独裁者|どくさいしゃ}が{国|くに}を{支配|しはい}した。
{独裁者|どくさいしゃ}は{言論|げんろん}の{自由|じゆう}を{奪|うば}った。
examples.english: The dictator took away freedom of speech.

examples.japanese: {歴史|れきし}の{中|なか}で{多|おお}くの{独裁者|どくさいしゃ}が{民衆|みんしゅう}の{反乱|はんらん}によって{倒|たお}されてきた。
examples.english: Throughout history, many dictators have been overthrown by popular uprisings.

notes:
USAGE:
{独裁者|どくさいしゃ} always carries a negative connotation. It is used in political, historical, and figurative contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {独裁者|どくさいしゃ}を{倒|たお}す (to overthrow a dictator)
- {独裁者|どくさいしゃ}の{支配|しはい} (a dictator's rule)
- {軍事|ぐんじ}{独裁者|どくさいしゃ} (military dictator)

WORD FORMATION:
{独裁|どくさい} (dictatorship) + {者|しゃ} (person). The base noun {独裁|どくさい} also appears in {独裁|どくさい}{政権|せいけん} (dictatorial regime) and {独裁|どくさい}{国家|こっか} (dictatorial state).
